citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
There are expired bottles of doxycycline and ponazuril stored in the refrigerator. Additionally, a bottle of ceftriaxone
injectable antibiotic with Russian manufacturing labeling was found. The Attending Veterinarian confirmed that this
product is not approved for use.
Expired medications present several significant risks, including reduced potency that may prevent the drug from achieving
its intended therapeutic effect, increasing the likelihood of treatment failure and prolonged or worsening clinical conditions.
The licensee must ensure all medications used for animals covered under the Animal Welfare Act are not expired and
approved by the Attending Veterinarian. Each dealer or exhibitor shall establish and maintain programs of adequate
veterinary care that include the use of appropriate methods to prevent, control, diagnose, and treat diseases and injuries,
and the availability of emergency, weekend, and holiday care. Correct this day, July 2, 2026, forward.

The facility failed to hold multiple cats for the 5 day period required in regulation § 2.101(a)(4). USDA inspectors reviewed
acquisition and disposition records for the month of May 2026 and found that 23 cats had been transferred to buyers
before the 5 day holding period.
Adequate holding periods are necessary to allow for observation of animals for signs of stress, disease or other conditions
that may be worsened by transport.
Any live dog or cat acquired by a dealer or exhibitor shall be held by him or her, under his or her supervision and control,
for a period of not less than 5 full days, not including the day of acquisition, after acquiring the animal, excluding time in
transit: Provided, however: any live dog or cat, 120 days of age or less, that was obtained from the person that bred and
raised such dog or cat, may be exempted from the 5-day holding requirement and may be disposed of by dealers or
exhibitors after a minimum holding period of 24 hours, excluding time in transit. Each subsequent dealer or exhibitor must
also hold each such dog or cat for a 24- hour period excluding time in transit.Correct this day, July 10, 2026, forward.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with facility representative.
Additional Inspectors:
Colette Kirk El-Amin, VETERINARY MEDICAL OFFICER n
